question: On non-contrast CT, an extradural haematoma (EDH) appears as a biconvex (lens-shaped) hyperdense collection that does NOT cross suture lines, whereas a subdural haematoma (SDH) appears as a crescentic hyperdense collection that conforms to the brain surface and can cross suture lines.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and is the single most tested CT head-injury fact. EDH = biconvex (lens) and does NOT cross sutures (dura adherent). SDH = crescentic, follows the brain surface and CAN cross sutures. Remembering the shape locks in the diagnosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The shape difference is the core CT discriminator: EDH is biconvex because the tightly adherent dura at suture lines limits spread; SDH is crescentic because blood tracks freely in the subdural space across sutures. EDH is classically from middle meningeal artery rupture; SDH from bridging veins. Both may require emergency craniotomy.
